synthesis: The source connects auxiliary-function design through two different objective regimes. An admissible trigonometric polynomial supplies b0, b1, and b and fixes theta; theta in turn determines the compactly supported autoconvolution smoother and the decomposition F(z)=f(0)/z+F0(z), whose bounded remainder enters the finite-height error budget. After Y and Y1 vanish asymptotically, the leading coefficient objective R2 remains, whereas the all-height objective R1 retains secondary terms. This makes the reported degree-46 R2 winner and degree-40 R1 winner a concrete consequence of optimizing different proof interfaces, not merely two mentions of polynomial search; the separate classical-region rerun also shows that changing the smoothing family changes a finite-height constant while holding other named ingredients fixed.
source_support: Unit u03 states the polynomial admissibility conditions and the distinct degree-40 and degree-46 aggregates used by Theorems 1.1 and 1.2. Unit u06 constructs theta from b0,b1, then g, w, f, and F, and isolates F0 with a C5(R) bound. Unit u11 takes the limit in which Y,Y1 tend to zero and derives the asymptotic coefficient objective using P46. Units u12-u13 turn positivity into a squared-modulus/autocorrelation invariant, optimize R2, and explicitly report that the degree-40 polynomial has a slightly worse R2 but the best R1 before further R1 refinement. Unit u14 reports a controlled rerun of the classical-region iteration in which replacing the h^(1) smoother by h^(4) worsens R0 from 5.5586904517 to 5.5608403.
nonparaphrase_operation: Compose the maps c -> autocorrelation coefficients b -> theta and smoothing transform F -> theorem-specific error expression, then compare what survives under the asymptotic limit with what remains in the all-height calculation. The composition identifies the polynomial and smoother as inputs to different retained error channels and predicts objective-specific winners.
limits: The source directly demonstrates the polynomial mismatch between R2 and R1 and a smoothing-family effect in the separate classical-region calculation; it does not isolate an independently optimal finite-height value of E, so no stronger claim about E's optimizer is warranted. Simulated annealing is heuristic, the rounded coefficient tables are not an optimality or admissibility certificate by themselves, and transform formulas, numerical constants, and the classical iteration remain formula/computation sensitive.
quality_reason: Accepted because the relation requires multiple distinct units: the representation and search units alone do not explain the theorem-level objective split, while the asymptotic and smoothing units alone do not establish the observed different polynomial winners. Together they give a concrete parameter-to-transform-to-error mechanism and an explicit finite-versus-asymptotic comparison, with the unsupported stronger E claim bounded away.

synthesis: The intermediate-region proof and the all-height contradiction form a producer-consumer interface that the future-work section generalizes. The fixed-line argument supplies a finite-height zero-free boundary; the main contradiction consumes that boundary on the short starting interval to certify the empty rectangle required by its detector, then uses monotone error bounds to exclude a counterexample at every larger height. Replacing this single handoff by successive boundaries nu_j yields an envelope construction in which each finite certificate supplies the precondition for the next stage.
source_support: Unit u10 proves Theorem 1.4's O(1/log t) region via a maximal-Y contradiction and states its use on the intermediate range exp(8928) to exp(52238). Unit u09 explicitly invokes Theorem 1.4 for t' in [T0-1,T0), combines it with the existing region above T0 to prove rectangle (5.5), verifies the hypotheses of Lemma 4.7, compresses the unbounded range using decreasing Y(t), and closes with M>0.04897601>M1. Unit u15 explicitly summarizes this finite-seed-to-all-larger-heights mechanism and proposes chaining boundary functions nu_j so their finite intervals form an envelope before the standard argument covers [T0,infinity).
nonparaphrase_operation: Treat a zero-free boundary as a typed certificate: its finite-interval output discharges the empty-rectangle precondition of the next detector argument, whose resulting boundary can be fed forward. This composition exposes the gap (10.1) as the exact failed interface obligation rather than as a generic lack of evidence.
limits: Only the u10-to-u09 handoff is established. The 355-stage envelope and constant 52.74 are proposed future work, conditional on excluding every narrow gap at heights roughly exp(40000) through exp(5*10^7); the source says current computation and zero-density estimates cannot do so. Exact inequalities, monotonicity, transforms, and numerical constants are formula/computation sensitive, and a failed gap certificate would break propagation.
quality_reason: Accepted because u10 and u09 exhibit a concrete cross-unit dependency, while u15 abstracts that verified dependency into a precise iterative mechanism and identifies its unresolved obstruction. No single parent contains both the finite boundary's construction, its use as the rectangle certificate in the global contradiction, and the conditional multi-stage envelope.
